title: Victor recordings, Lonely Melody and Whiteman's arrangers
summary: He discusses Victor and later Columbia sessions in this period and who arranged what, including Satterfield and Lenny Hayden.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No. Now, at the same time you were writing different things for Whiteman, I am familiar with a couple of things that have been reissued, which feature Bix and Bix and Trumbauer. I know the one thing, Lonely Melody." Lovely thing.
When was that, was that right around that time or was that a little later?

This came -- we did that at Victor, and see, it was not too long after this maybe a year that we changed -- Whiteman changed his affiliation from the Victor over to the Columbia. Now, this was still in the Victor contract. We were still making recordings, arrangements, now mostly over at Lederkrautz. This is where we were doing most of the recording. And then we'd come around and we were working pretty much out of New York, but they're going on the road and in the beginning of this season, I think -- I don't know when we got the Old Gold -- I think that was later, that was later.
But anyway, there's Old Man River, Lonely Melody." We got down to Camden and made a few down there.
Are those the ones with Crosby that Bix and Trumbauer kind of chase choruses on 'You Took Advantage of Me.' Did you do that arrangement?
No, no. Tommy Satterfield, he was in the band then. Very fine arranger, but he didn't stay too long, but then after he left they got Lenny Hayden.
Yeah, but now that I guess that is a whole year in there, that comes in. Anyway I had any number of things that worked out with Bix, but Bix being away I did some of these three-trumpet things.
He went in and out of the band.
No, no, he was in the band, but the band was in and out of New York.
Oh, in and out of New York, I see.
I stayed in New York, Ferde was over in Jersey, and let's see, we went along about a whole year like that before we changed over to the Columbia. I think -- a little mixed up --
